probe_assessment: The cold read held up for the module purpose and every listed public API item. Three listed stumbles are genuine comprehension traps: the live boundary row delegates eligibility and ranking to selection helpers whose criteria are not defined here; _settings encodes an implicit presence/rank/value ordering contract with no local explanation or consumer; and the clean/contained calculations depend on return and ground-truth shapes supplied by imported functions. These are file-hopping or implicit-contract problems, not material errors in the probe's purpose or API summary.

probe_findings.claim: The live boundary row's eligibility filter and ranking rule are delegated to selection helpers whose criteria are not defined in sweep.py, so a junior cannot resolve this choice from the file alone.
probe_findings.quote:

        selection.coverage_allowance_rows(rows, n_rallies),

probe_findings.claim: The purpose and ordering contract of _settings are not recoverable from sweep.py: the function builds presence and hard-coded strategy-rank pairs, but the file does not explain why those ranks exist or where the tuple is consumed.

The clean and contained calculations rely on the undocumented return shape of classify_all and the extent tuple shape of ground-truth rallies; a junior cannot fully resolve what those counts mean from this file alone.
probe_findings.quote:
clean = [(index, rally, span) for index, (rally, (kind, span)) in enumerate(zip(gt, classifications)) if kind is RallyBoundary.COVERED and span not in merged]
    offsets = [abs(spans[span][0] - rally.extent[0]) for _index, rally, span in clean]
    contained = [sum(start <= first and last < end for first, last in (r.extent for r in gt)) for start, end in spans]

verdicts.suggested_fix: Rename it to _report_withheld_verdict or _print_to_both so the output behaviour is explicit.
verdicts.verifier_note: The naming and style-lens claims concern the same helper and are merged. The call sites explain that the verdict is withheld, but the helper name still does not signal that it emits the message twice.

verdicts.claim: _row_for_result combines ground-truth loading, boundary scoring, alignment calculations, contact scoring, report-row construction and split-log generation in one broad helper.
verdicts.quote:
def _row_for_result(fixture: Fixture, spec: CandidateSpec, result: Any, master: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    gt = load_gt_rallies(master, fixture.video_id)
    spans = result.spans
    boundary = score_boundaries(spans, gt)
    classifications = classify_all(spans, gt)
    merged = merged_span_indices(spans, gt)
verdicts.suggested_fix: Group metric calculations behind a few focused helpers or document the result-row sections so the related and diagnostic outputs are easy to distinguish.
verdicts.verifier_note: All work feeds one candidate result row, so the concern is breadth rather than wholly unrelated module responsibilities. The boundary, contact, alignment and split-log sections are nevertheless distinct enough to create onboarding friction.
